s1.syndrome_frame: liver mass with possible metastasis in a patient with history of colon cancer
salient_findings: 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
liver tumor with solid and cystic components
absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
key_facts: 55-year-old man
history of right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
no thrombophilic disorders
normal preoperative CEA and CA19-9 levels
completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
13 months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a liver lesion
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
liver tumor with two components: solid and cystic
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of colon cancer and liver lesion with solid and cystic components

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver tumor with two components and absence of right portal vein

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver mass and history of colon cancer, which increases risk of cholangiocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic component of liver tumor and potential connection to biliary tree

shortlist.label: Sarcomatoid hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature of tumor and potential for sarcomatoid transformation

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, staged as IIIB, and the liver lesion was found 13 months after surgery, which is consistent with metastasis from the primary colon cancer.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers including α-fetoprotein and PIVKA-II, and no evidence of hepatitis B or C infection, make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: No communication with the biliary tree and negative bile cytology for malignancy make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of a solid component in the liver tumor and the patient's history of colon cancer make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Sarcomatoid hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's history and the characteristics of the liver tumor do not support this rare and aggressive variant of hepatocellular carcinoma
